author: Peyton Gay
title: Jackson County students can take their driving exam at school - NewsBreak
text:
By Peyton Gay ,
7 hours ago
JACKSON COUNTY, Fla. ( WMBB ) – Students enrolled in driver’s education at any of the high schools in Jackson County will soon be able to take their driver’s test on campus.
District officials want to make learning to drive and getting a license as simple as doing your homework, while taking some of the stress off parents.
“Driving is kind of like doing your homework. And as a parent, you realize helping your kids with their homework, sometimes you would rather, I mean, that’s like pulling teeth sometimes. So it gives us the opportunity to teach the students how to drive in a maybe a less pressure situation,” Driver’s Education Director Carlan Martin said.
One of the main goals is to help students feel more comfortable while taking the test.
“You think about it, if you’re climbing in a car to go test and you’re getting in there with a stranger that you don’t know, that sitting over there you’re already going to be nervous as it is, but then that compounds that makes it even that much more. Whereas we’re teaching them how to drive, we’re teaching them the skills that they need to pass that test. So they’re going to get used to us, and they’re going to be more comfortable with us,” Martin said.
After the test has been administered, all the student has to do is visit the DMV to get their license.
“It’s time for them to go get their license. They can go to the DMV that will pull them up on the computer and verify all the information that we put in there. And then they’ll have to take their vision test, and they can get their license,” Martin said.
District officials say that bringing driver’s education back to the schools has been a top priority.
Now, they are happy to be expanding that service.
“Jackson County is rated pretty high in the state with teen fatalities. And really and truly, it’s one of the few things that we can do at the school level that we provide a community service,” Martin said.
The district plans to start administering tests next week; they already have the first student at Marianna High School signed up.
